column1: # ADR-0034 D2 — the email normaliser's shared case table (R3#5 / R4#2).
# One implementation is Go (internal/authpolicy NormalizeEmail); platform has a
# shell one (scripts/lib/roster.sh roster_normalize_email). They must agree on
# every row. This file is read by BOTH test suites; a row that one side
# disagrees with is a bug in that side, not a reason to drop the row.
#   - blank lines and lines starting with `#` are ignored
#   - split each line on its FIRST tab only. `input` may be empty (the line then
#     starts with a tab) and may contain spaces; neither column ever contains a
#     tab or a newline. Do NOT read it with `IFS=$'\t' read` (tab is IFS
#     whitespace: a leading empty field collapses) — use awk -F'\t' or cut.
#   - `expect` is the normalised email, or the literal REJECT
#   - `{G0}` / `{G1}` stand for the two folded Google domains
#     (gmail.com / googlemail.com). They are substituted in BOTH columns before
#     use. Written as placeholders because scripts/check-emails.sh forbids a
#     mailbox-shaped literal on a public domain in any tracked file.
#   - every other address is on a reserved domain (local / test / invalid /
# The platform-side reader should be strict: an unparsable row, or a file with
# fewer than the Go side's minimum row count, is a FAIL, never a skip.
# --- accepted: a non-Google domain is only lower-cased (dots and +tag kept)
# --- accepted: the two Google domains fold (dots and +tag dropped, domain unified to the first)
# --- rejected: no @, an empty side, or more than one @
# --- rejected: a space inside the address
# --- rejected: non-ASCII, checked BEFORE case folding (U+212A KELVIN SIGN lower-cases to k)
# --- rejected: a domain with an empty label (trailing dot, leading dot, doubled dot)
# --- rejected: nothing left of the local part after Google folding
